issues.legal_issue: Authority delegated to issue a declaration also includes authority to conduct the prescribed preliminary inquiry.
material_facts: The State Government authorized an administrative officer to exercise its power to declare a local area a gram or nagar.
The officer conducted the prescribed inquiry before issuing the declaration.
issues.conclusion: The authorization to issue the declaration was sufficient to authorize the officer to conduct the inquiry preliminary to it.
issues.legal_principle: The power to make a declaration necessarily carries the power to make the inquiry preliminary to that declaration, because a declaration under section 9(1) cannot be made without an inquiry. The authorization under section 321 to exercise the power of declaration was therefore sufficient.

predicates.challenge_to_declaration: A party challenged a declaration made about a local area.
predicates.officer_authorized_to_declare: The government authorized an officer to exercise its power to make the declaration.
predicates.preliminary_inquiry_required: The law required an inquiry before the declaration could be made.

issues.definition: When a declaration is challenged in a proceeding and an authorized officer must make a preliminary inquiry, the authorization to declare includes authority to conduct that inquiry.

issues.legal_issue: A municipal borough may qualify as an administrative unit whose area can be declared a gram or nagar.
material_facts: The declaration covered the whole area within the limits of an existing municipal borough.

The statute provided that a local area co-extensive with or included within a municipal district or borough could be declared a gram or nagar, and that the municipality would cease to exist in the area after such a declaration.
issues.conclusion: A municipal borough is an administrative unit within the scope of section 9(1), and an area co-extensive with or included in it may be declared a gram or nagar.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 9 and 307 of the Gujarat Panchayats Act, read together, show that a municipal borough is an administrative unit within section 9(1), and that a local area co-extensive with or included within a municipal borough may be declared a gram or nagar.

predicates.challenge_to_declaration: A party challenged a declaration made about a local area.
predicates.area_is_municipal_unit: The area subject to the declaration is a municipal district, borough, or part of one.
predicates.statute_covers_included_or_coextensive_a: The governing law permits an area co-extensive with or included within a municipal unit to be declared a local self-government unit.

issues.definition: If a challenged declaration concerns a municipal area and the governing law covers areas co-extensive with or included within municipal units, that area may be declared a local self-government unit.

issues.legal_issue: A declaration is not mala fide merely because it follows a municipality's refusal to include surrounding areas in its limits.
material_facts: The municipality indicated that it was unwilling to include surrounding areas within its limits.
The government had consulted the municipality and had power to alter municipal limits without its consent.
The declaration covered the existing municipal area and did not include the surrounding areas at issue.
The record did not show how the declaration would benefit the alleged political actors, and the allegation of mala fides was denied.
issues.conclusion: The declaration was not shown to have been issued mala fide.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered the government's independent statutory power to alter municipal limits after consultation, the fact that the surrounding areas were not included in the declaration, and the absence of evidence showing an improper motive. Those circumstances did not establish mala fides.

rule.if: challenge_to_declaration and alleged_improper_motive and surrounding_area_not_included and no_evidence_of_personal_gain

predicates.challenge_to_declaration: A party challenged a declaration made about a local area.
predicates.alleged_improper_motive: The challenger alleged that the declaration was made for an improper purpose.
predicates.surrounding_area_not_included: The declaration did not include the surrounding area said to be the object of the alleged improper purpose.
predicates.no_evidence_of_personal_gain: The record contained no evidence that the alleged beneficiaries would gain from the declaration.

issues.definition: When an improper motive is alleged in a challenge to a declaration, the allegation is not established on these facts if the targeted surrounding area was excluded and no personal gain is evidenced.

issues.legal_issue: The power to declare local areas as grams or nagars under section 9(1) is not an excessive delegation of legislative power.
material_facts: The statute set population ranges for gram and nagar areas and authorized prescribed inquiries into population, land revenue, and whether areas could conveniently be grouped.

The statute's stated purpose was democratic decentralization through a system of local panchayats, and the court found that it contemplated establishing panchayats within a reasonable time in local areas with populations not exceeding 30,000, subject to specified exclusions.
The challenged area had a population of 12,249 and was declared a nagar after the prescribed inquiry.
issues.conclusion: Section 9(1) did not suffer from excessive delegation, and the declaration was lawful.
issues.legal_principle: An essential legislative function is the determination of legislative policy and its formulation as a binding rule; after laying down that policy, the legislature may leave administrative agencies discretion to execute it and work out details. The court applied In re Delhi Laws Act and Raj Narain Singh v. Chairman, Patna Administration Committee. It held that the Act's policy of establishing panchayats in eligible local areas guided and controlled the discretion under section 9(1); the possibility of abuse in administration did not make the provision unconstitutional.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_declaration_power and legislative_policy_guides_local_units and population_criteria_set and inquiry_confines_administrative_details

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_declaration_: A party challenged the legislature's delegation of authority to designate local self-government areas.
predicates.legislative_policy_guides_local_units: The law states a policy of establishing local self-government units in eligible areas.
predicates.population_criteria_set: The law specifies population criteria for the categories of local self-government units.
predicates.inquiry_confines_administrative_details: The required inquiry concerns factual and administrative matters needed to implement the statutory scheme.

issues.definition: A delegation is not excessive when a challenged designation power is guided by a stated local-government policy, population criteria, and inquiries confined to implementation details.

issues.legal_issue: The power to reorganize gram and nagar areas under section 9(2) is not an excessive delegation of legislative power.
material_facts: Section 9(2) authorized alteration of the limits of grams and nagars, inclusion or exclusion of local areas, and termination of a gram or nagar designation after consultation with specified panchayats.
The Act provided for establishment or reconstitution of panchayats and for amalgamation or division of areas following such changes.
No action under section 9(2) had been taken against the appellants.
issues.conclusion: Section 9(2) was not unconstitutional for excessive delegation.
issues.legal_principle: The legislature may leave administrative discretion over details needed to implement its policy. The court held that reorganization into new local self-government units could require inclusion, exclusion, alteration, amalgamation, division, or termination, and that not every contingency could be anticipated. The statutory consultation requirement and related provisions governing consequential changes supported the delegation.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_reorganizati: A party challenged a government's power to alter the boundaries or status of local self-government areas.
predicates.law_requires_consultation: The law requires consultation with relevant local bodies before the government exercises the reorganization power.
predicates.consequential_reorganization_provisions_: The law provides for consequences such as reconstitution, amalgamation, or division of local bodies after boundary or status changes.
predicates.reorganization_serves_local_self_governm: The reorganization power is directed to forming or arranging units of local self-government.

issues.definition: A reorganization delegation is not excessive when it serves local self-government, requires consultation, and is accompanied by provisions addressing the consequences of reorganization.

issues.legal_issue: The government cannot rely solely on an unsupported population classification to leave eligible municipalities outside the statutory panchayat scheme.
material_facts: The government adopted a policy distinguishing municipalities within the statutory population range and left some municipalities unconverted on that basis.
The statute placed all local areas with populations exceeding 10,000 but not exceeding 30,000 on the same footing for designation as nagars.

The court held that the policy classification was not justified by the statute and that, if non-conversion rested solely on that policy, the government had a duty to establish panchayats in the affected municipalities as soon as possible.
The challenged declaration concerned an area with a population of 12,249 and was not invalidated by the non-conversion of other municipalities.
issues.conclusion: The government's population-based classification was unlawful insofar as it departed from the statutory scheme; non-conversion based solely on that classification was unjustified, but it did not invalidate the challenged declaration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(1) placed all local areas in the statutory range of more than 10,000 and not more than 30,000 on the same footing. A government policy creating unsupported subcategories could not justify non-conversion contrary to that scheme. The court nevertheless held that the failure to convert other municipalities did not vitiate the declaration under challenge.

predicates.challenge_to_nonconversion: A party challenged the government's failure to bring an eligible municipality into the local self-government scheme.
predicates.population_within_statutory_nagar_range: The area's population falls within the range that the governing law treats as eligible for the same local-unit category.
predicates.nonconversion_based_only_on_population_s: The government left the area outside the scheme solely because of a population subcategory not established by the governing law.

issues.definition: When an eligible area's non-conversion rests solely on a population subcategory not recognized by the governing scheme, that non-conversion is unjustified.
